newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo court jails collapsed building owner 7 years.
newsitem.headline: Cairo court jails collapsed building owner 7 years.

text.p: A Cairo court on Wednesday sentenced to seven years in jail with hard labour the owner of an apartment block that collapsed last year, crushing to death 64 people and injuring 16.

The prosecutor had charged owner Raouf Ibrahim Wissa with causing the death of the residents by disregarding the design plans and constructing faulty supports. He was also charged with constructing five illegal floors on top of the building.
The court sentenced architects Ahmed Riyad and Ashraf el-Magary to three years in jail with hard labour and fined them 325,000 pounds ($98,000) each.
It acquitted Abdel Aziz Khodeir, who was helping the two men remodel a flat on the first floor. All three were charged with removing vital supports and pillars.
The 11-storey building, in the Cairo suburb of Heliopolis, collapsed into a mountain of rubble in late October.
The collapse, one of the worst to happen in Cairo, prompted the government to introduce mandatory jail sentences for illegally adding floors or renovating a building.
